newsitem.title: CANADA: Stone tenders for outstanding debt series.
newsitem.headline: Stone tenders for outstanding debt series.

text.p: Stone-Consolidated Corp said on Friday it had begun a tender offer and consent solicitation for its outstanding 10.25 percent senior secured notes due 2000 and its 10-3/4 percent secured notes due 2001.

The purpose of the offering was to reduce the company's total interest expense by replacing notes with bank loans, the company said. The aim of the solicitation was to amend or eliminate substantially all of the restrictive provisions and covenants relating to the notes, it said.
This would improve the company's operating and financial flexibility, Stone said.

In conjunction with the tender offer, Stone said it was soliciting note holder consent at the close of business on April 17 of a majority of the outstanding principal amount of each series of notes to propose amendments to the indenture for each series.
The proposed amendments would amend or eliminate substantially all of the restrictive covenants and certain default provisions of each debt, the company said.
On February 14, Canadian newsprint companies Stone-Consolidated and Abitibi-Price Inc announced they agreed to merge in an all-stock transaction.
Stone-Consolidated said it planned to fund payment of the tender offer consideration through an advance under a bridge credit facility arranged in connection with its merger with Abitibi-Price.
